name: Óenach

attributes.attribute: mixed markets and games with sacred rites
lit on the hilltop at Uisneach

sources: Aitchison, N. B. Armagh and the Royal Centres in Early Medieval Ireland: Monuments, Cosmology and the Past. Rochester, N.Y.: Crithne Press/Boydell & Brewer, 1994.
Raftery, Brian. Pagan Celtic Ireland: The Enigma of the Irish Iron Age. London: Thames and Hudson, 1994, 81 ff.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Óenach was a fair and festival at Uisneach. It happened every Beltane, on May 1. Markets and games filled the day around the sacred rites. People lit twin fires on the hilltop. That fire lighting was part of the deeper ceremony.

okr.objective: The Óenach is the Beltane festival held at Uisneach.
key_results: The Óenach took place at Uisneach every Beltane, on May 1.
Markets and games ran alongside the sacred rites.
People lit twin fires on the hilltop as part of the ceremony.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
